subject: Renewal discussion: rate cushion, true-up options, and SLA credits
messages:
From: Samantha Li <samantha.li@atlashealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@atlashealth.com
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal window and pricing alignment

Karthik —

Hope you’re well. Our contract with Redwood is up for renewal in April and usage has grown materially across our clinical inference pipelines. Procurement asked me to open a conversation around how we can keep unit economics predictable while we scale. Two specific asks from our side: 1) a short-term rate hold for Q2 to avoid sudden price exposure while we finish a multi-month migration; 2) a clearer true-up cadence (monthly vs quarterly) and a cushion of credits if we exceed committed throughput during peak testing.

I attached our Q4 usage export so you can see the trend. Can we set a call this week for a concrete proposal? Happy to include our finance lead if useful.

Thanks,
Samantha Li
Director, Cloud Procurement
Atlas Health
(415) 555-0190

Attachments: Atlas_Usage_Q4_2026.csv (attachment/csv)

From: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Li <samantha.li@atlashealth.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 11:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal window and pricing alignment

Samantha —

Appreciate the heads-up and the data. I reviewed the Q4 export; growth is clear and we want to make renewal smooth for you. Quick thoughts before a call:

- Short-term rate hold: we can offer a 90-day rate stabilization for Q2 on your current committed tier, conditional on a modest committed uplift (10% over current commit) to cover baseline growth.
- Credits cushion: propose a 25% overage credit for spikes above committed throughput during the hold window, applied as usage credits on the next invoice (not cash).
- True-up cadence: we prefer monthly true-ups for accuracy; we can automate invoice smoothing so you don’t hit single-month spikes hard.
- SLA credit language: we can introduce a one-time SLA credit for any priority incidents during the stabilization period.

I’ve looped in Monica (renewals) and Marissa (pricing ops) to confirm internal approvals and to prepare a pricing overlay. Can you do a 30-min call tomorrow (Thu) at 10am PT?

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com

From: monica_patel@redwoodinference.com <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 08:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal window and pricing alignment

Karthik —

Thanks for drafting. Internal constraints to flag: our standard stabilization offer requires an uplift of at least 15% for enterprise accounts if we’re guaranteeing a price hold longer than 60 days. Given Atlas’ growth and strategic profile, I’m comfortable exceptions: we can go 90 days at 10% uplift but need an explicit clause that allows us to move them up to the next commit tier if sustained usage >120% for two consecutive months after the hold.

Also recommend we present two flavors:
- Option A (Conservative): 90-day rate hold, 15% committed uplift, 15% overage credits for spikes, monthly true-up.
- Option B (Customer-first): 90-day rate hold, 10% committed uplift, 25% overage credits, automatic monthly true-up and one-time SLA credit up to $10k equivalent.

I’ll review the pricing overlay and authorize Option B if Marissa confirms margin math.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Head of Renewals — Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwoodinference.com

From: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com, monica_patel@redwoodinference.com, Samantha Li <samantha.li@atlashealth.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 09:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Proposed overlay and ask for confirmation

Hi all —

Attached is Proposed_Pricing_Overlay_v3.xlsx with the two options broken into per-token economics, projected monthly true-up impacts, and an estimated fiscal impact to Atlas for Q2. Key callouts:

- Option A: preserves our margin better but requires a 15% uplift; projected invoice smoothing reduces month-to-month variance by ~28%.
- Option B: moves faster from a customer-retention POV; margin hit is manageable with forecasted usage and can be offset by a 6-month step-up to baseline commit after the stabilization window.

SLA credit language is in SLA_Credit_Terms.pdf — this is a one-time credit, not recurring.

Samantha — if you confirm Option B, I’ll prepare a one-page amendment and send to DocuSign (we’ll include the auto-trueup automation and a 90-day clause).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Pricing Manager — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: Proposed_Pricing_Overlay_v3.xlsx (attachment/xlsx), SLA_Credit_Terms.pdf (attachment/pdf)

Date: Wed, 17 Feb 2027 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Proposed overlay and ask for confirmation

Karthik / Monica / Marissa —

Thanks for the clear options and the overlays — very helpful. We discussed with finance and legal. Atlas is willing to accept Option B with one small change: we need the monthly true-up to include a two-week usage averaging window (so a single anomalous week doesn’t immediately push us to the next tier). Also, can you include the one-time SLA credit as a line item in the amendment (for transparency on our side to auditors)?

If you can update the one-page amendment with that averaging language and the SLA credit line item, we can sign. Please send via DocuSign and copy procurement@atlashealth.com. Looking to close this week.

Best,
Samantha Li
Director, Cloud Procurement
Atlas Health
